question: Can a stronger LLM generating query-specific reasoning traces automatically turn zero-shot prompts into few-shot CoT-style prompts that improve a weaker LLM on multi-step implicit reasoning?
hypothesis: Query-specific rationales generated by a stronger model improve a weaker model's accuracy over zero-shot and fixed-exemplar CoT, especially on implicit multi-step reasoning (StrategyQA).
contributions: A two-tier approach where a stronger LLM generates reasoning traces for a weaker LLM
Improved performance on complex reasoning tasks, particularly implicit reasoning
Insights into interaction between advanced LLMs and structured prompting, including regressions
A framework toward more robust and interpretable AI reasoning systems

method.summary: Two-step pipeline: GPT-4 (1106-preview) is prompted with a template containing two decomposition exemplars and the question and writes reasoning traces (sub-questions) without answering; the question plus traces are then given to GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106 to produce the final answer. Compared with a base prompt and a fixed 3-exemplar CoT prompt on HotpotQA and StrategyQA.
method.task: multi-step question answering (yes/no and short answer)

datasets.name: HotpotQA
datasets.split: random subset of N=20 per run, resampled each run

datasets.name: StrategyQA
datasets.size: over 570 unique categories (as printed; no question count)
datasets.split: random subset of N=20 per run, resampled each run

models.name: GPT-4-1106-preview (rationale generator; Algorithm 1 calls it gpt-4-turbo-1106)

other.note: the paper does not say whether GPT-4-Turbo answerer rationales come from the same GPT-4 model

inference.samples: N=20 questions per run, 3 runs with fresh shuffle, average of 3 run scores
inference.prompting: AutoReason: generator prompt with 2 decomposition exemplars (zero tuning), then answer prompt with question+rationales (the final-answer template is said to be in the appendix but is not printed). CoT baseline: 3 fixed exemplars (hamsters, Brooke Shields, Hydrogen/Spice Girls). Base: instruction-only prompt.

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: percentage of questions answered correctly 'according to decision boundary'; an LLM scorer rates each answer 0-10 against the gold answer (threshold not stated)

eval.protocol: 3 runs of 20 shuffled-sampled questions, averaged; no significance test, no variance reported

prompts.text: You will formulate Chain of Thought (CoT) reasoning traces. CoT is a prompting technique that helps you to think about a problem in a structured way. It breaks down a problem into a series of logical reasoning traces. You will be given a question and using this question you will decompose the question into a series of logical reasoning traces. Only write the reasoning traces and do not answer the question yourself. Here are some examples of CoT reasoning traces: Question: Did Brazilian jiu-jitsu Gracie founders have at least a baker's dozen of kids between them? Reasoning traces: - Who were the founders of Brazilian jiu-jitsu? - What is the number represented by the baker's dozen? - How many children do Gracie founders have altogether - Is this number bigger than baker's dozen? Question: Is cow methane safer for environment than cars Reasoning traces: - How much methane is produced by cars annually? - How much methane is produced by cows annually? - Is methane produced by cows less than methane produced by cars? Question: ${question} Reasoning traces:

You're an agent. Your job is to answer some questions. Here are the rules: 1. You will be given a question 2. You will answer the question with a short answer, it might yes/no or a short phrase 3. When you know the answer, write it in this format only: "<answer>"

You're an agent. Your job is to answer some questions. Here are the rules: 1. You will be given a question 2. You will answer the question with true or false 3. When you know the answer, write it in this format only: "answer"

Your job is to score an answer's correctness from 0 to 10. You will be given the question, the correct answer, and the answer you need to score. 0 means the answer is completely wrong, 10 means the answer is completely correct. Explain your reasoning first shortly, and then write the score as a literal number (0 to 10).

results.claim: AutoReason lifts GPT-3.5-Turbo on StrategyQA over base and CoT
results.setup: StrategyQA, N=20 random questions per run, 3 runs averaged, GPT-4-1106-preview writes rationales, GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106 answers; base 55.0, CoT 70.3
results.quote:
GPT-3.5-Turbo, when used with AutoReason achieved an accuracy of
76.6%, surpassing its base performance of 55% and the CoT performance of 70.3%.

results.claim: GPT-4-Turbo on StrategyQA rises from base to CoT to AutoReason
results.quote:
GPT-4’s reasoning
accuracy increased form 71.6% (base) to 76.6% (CoT) to an impressive 91.6% when using AutoReason.

results.claim: On HotpotQA AutoReason lifts GPT-3.5-Turbo while plain CoT lowers it
results.setup: HotpotQA, N=20 random questions per run, 3 runs averaged; GPT-3.5-Turbo base 61.6, CoT 58.3
results.quote:
GPT-3.5-Turbo’s accuracy increased on all counts from 61.6% (base) to 76.6% on
AutoReason, and surprisingly decreased to 58.3% on normal CoT.

results.claim: GPT-4-Turbo on HotpotQA: AutoReason is below base but above CoT
results.setup: HotpotQA, N=20 random questions per run, 3 runs averaged; GPT-4-Turbo base 73.3, CoT 63.3
results.where: Text (Sec 3.1) places the '1.7% drop' and the 'drop by 10% to 63.4' under StrategyQA wording, but the numbers match Table 1 (HotpotQA: 73.3 -> 71.6, CoT 63.3). Table prints 63.3, text prints 63.4. Text on StrategyQA says GPT-4 base 71.6, which is also the HotpotQA AutoReason figure.
results.quote:
a regression from base prompting to
AutoReason prompting was observed on GPT4

results.claim: Standard CoT hurt GPT-4-Turbo on HotpotQA relative to base
results.setup: HotpotQA, N=20 random questions per run, 3 runs averaged; GPT-4-Turbo CoT vs base 73.3

limits: Only 20 questions per run and 3 runs: no variance or significance test; the authors concede the limited sample size and number of runs
Only two QA datasets and one model family (OpenAI); authors call for broader tasks
Scoring uses an unnamed LLM scorer with an unstated 'decision boundary'; scorer bias not examined
Compares only to base and a 3-shot CoT; no comparison with Auto-CoT, Active Prompt or self-consistency, which it discusses
Gain is confounded with a stronger model supplying the reasoning (GPT-4 rationales to GPT-3.5), so it is not a pure prompting gain; the authors note cost of two LLM calls
GPT-4-Turbo regresses on HotpotQA (73.3 -> 71.6); authors say they lack definitive evidence for why
Final-answer prompt template is referred to as in the appendix but is not printed; decoding settings absent
Text and tables disagree in places (dataset attribution of regression, 63.3 vs 63.4); the HotpotQA CoT prompt A.3 is identical to the StrategyQA CoT A.5
Rationale quality is crucial; poor rationales can cause wrong answers or hallucinations
